document_contents.quote: In paragraph ‘11’ of the SCN, it was observed that the petitioner had contravened the provisions of the Act of 1994 and rules made thereunder with an intent to evade the payment of service tax.

It was submitted that the licensing is in two parts. One part is to sell food to passengers in trains as per norms and standards of the Railways and the another is renting of base kitchen and other property of the Railways.

The adjudicating authority, however, held that the Indian Railways provided “support services” to the licensee and these services are taxable by virtue of not being covered under Section 66D and service taxes payable on the licensee of reverse charge basis.

defects_argued.quote: A question has been raised as to whether all the periods covered under the demand Show Cause Notice (in short ‘SCN’) dated 16.04.2019 is well within statutory limitation period.

outcome.quote: This writ application stands disposed of accordingly.
